prompt_text:
Task: Pub/Sub Messaging

Write code that publishes a batch of messages with IDs or attributes using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Google Cloud Pub/Sub:
  Service: Cloud Pub/Sub
  SDK: google-cloud-pubsub
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: PublisherClient.publish, SubscriberClient
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview

Option 2 — Amazon SNS/SQS:
  Service: Amazon SNS and SQS
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish, send_message, receive_message
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html

Option 3 — Confluent:
  Service: Confluent Cloud Kafka
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: CONFLUENT_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, CONFLUENT_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/client-apps.html

Option 4 — Alibaba MNS / RocketMQ:
  Service: Alibaba Cloud Message Service / RocketMQ
  SDK: alibabacloud_mns / rocketmq
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish_message, send_message
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/message-service

Option 5 — IBM Event Streams:
  Service: IBM Event Streams
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_BROKERS, IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_APIKEY
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/EventStreams

Option 6 — Azure Service Bus:
  Service: Azure Service Bus
  SDK: azure-servicebus
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: send_messages, receive_messages
  Setup hints: AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import os
from azure.servicebus import ServiceBusClient, ServiceBusMessage

def publish_batch_messages(connection_string: str, queue_name: str, messages_data: list[tuple[str, dict]]):
    """
    Publishes a batch of messages to an Azure Service Bus queue.

    Args:
        connection_string: The connection string for the Azure Service Bus namespace.
        queue_name: The name of the queue to publish messages to.
        messages_data: A list of tuples, where each tuple contains
                       (message_body: str, attributes: dict).
                       The attributes dictionary will be mapped to application properties.
    """
    with ServiceBusClient.from_connection_string(connection_string) as client:
        sender = client.get_queue_sender(queue_name=queue_name)
        with sender:
            message_batch = sender.create_message_batch()
            for body, attributes in messages_data:
                message = ServiceBusMessage(body)
                if attributes:
                    message.application_properties = attributes
                try:
                    message_batch.add_message(message)
                except ValueError:
                    # Batch is full, send it and start a new one
                    sender.send_messages(message_batch)
                    message_batch = sender.create_message_batch()
                    message_batch.add_message(message)
            if message_batch:
                sender.send_messages(message_batch)

# Example usage (assuming connection string and queue name are set as environment variables or passed in)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Replace with your actual connection string and queue name
    # It's recommended to load these from environment variables or a secure configuration
    sb_connection_string = os.environ.get("AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING")
    sb_queue_name = os.environ.get("AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME", "myqueue")

    if not sb_connection_string:
        print("Please set the AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING environment variable.")
    else:
        messages_to_publish = [
            ("Hello from message 1", {"message_id": "msg-001", "type": "greeting"}),
            ("This is message 2", {"message_id": "msg-002", "priority": "high"}),
            ("Another message here", {"message_id": "msg-003", "source": "app_x"}),
            ("Final message in batch", {"message_id": "msg-004", "status": "processed"})
        ]
        try:
            publish_batch_messages(sb_connection_string, sb_queue_name, messages_to_publish)
            print(f"Published {len(messages_to_publish)} messages to Azure Service Bus queue '{sb_queue_name}'.")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"An error occurred: {e}")
